Wow, reading comprehension. He did NOT say "donating to charity is net negative." Did you even listen to the clip?

He says, very clearly, "I have my money in a donor-advised fund (DAF) and I try to put money towards things I think are helping civilization."

What is a DAF? A DAF is a charitable vehicle managed directly by a donor that CAN ONLY DONATE TO 501C(3) CHARITIES. A DAF is not a slush fund that you can use to invest into your friends' startups, you have to donate the money to an accredited nonprofit.

He is not criticizing "charity" in this clip. He is criticizing "Philanthropy" (capital P) in the form of self-perpetuating foundations made in their founder's names, which, he argues, only exist to keep existing, and ultimately lose sight of their original missions.

He criticizes SOME charities as being ideological and counterproductive (he alludes to the famous case of Scared Straight programs, which were found to actually increase rates of criminality). But that's not the same as saying "donating to all charity is negative." He just wants to make the decision for himself, rather than deferring to a foundation staffed by nonprofit drones.

He's still donating to charities, just ones he chooses. That's what a DAF is versus a foundation.

If you're looking for a "don't donate to charity" clip, or even a "billionaires are evil" clip, you picked the wrong one.

Majors pump.

↓

Shorts get liquidated. The squeeze sends prices higher.

↓

Prices keep climbing. Confidence slowly returns.

↓

↓

↓

FOMO kicks in. Sideliners start buying.

↓

Profits from majors flow into riskier assets and leveraged longs.

↓

Bigger wins, more PnL sharing, more people chasing.

↓

Winning feels easy. Leverage amounts progress.

↓

Everyone raises their targets instead of taking profits.

↓

The first dump gets bought. The bounce brings another wave of FOMO.

↓

More shorts get liquidated. Bears are fcked. Bulls are in control.

↓

The next dip barely bounces. Trading gets harder.

↓

Overleveraged longs get liquidated. Forced selling triggers more liquidations.

↓

PnL screenshots are getting rarer. It's now liquidation data.

↓

FOMO flips from fear of missing gains to fear of losing what’s left.

↓

Everyone turns bearish again.

$SIVE ER transcript just dropped, TLDR:

- 6 NEW pluggable players working with Sivers now.

Probably the biggest news of the entire ER next to new foundry allocations. 

"3 are in alpha sample evaluation stage" and another 3 in technical engagement / supply assessment stage."

And now it makes more sense why their $1.2B revenue pipeline ballooned (since this was a bigger leap than Jabil). 

- Initial production orders with $JBL expected in the first half of 2027, with the production ramp planned second half of 2027

LFG, Jabil is a massive hyperscaler supplier and finally got clear timelines on revenue from volume ramp.

- "new foundry partner who has brought on tremendous capacity that is available now"

This is what I wanted to hear. Apparently they've been in the works for this for awhile since it's "available now", and THIS IS VERY MATERIAL. 

CW lasers are in a massive shortage and $SIVE brought on new supply outside of Win Semi (also de-risks).

As you hear with other qualified CW players (anything they make gets sold), so as Sivers partners finishes their qualifications, I'm expecting the same.

- "long-term capacity model where one-third of manufacturing capacity will be internal, while two-thirds will come from our foundry partners"

Lukewarm on this, it makes sense they need to be vertically integrated like $AAOI / $LITE eventually but implies more capex (better after NASDAQ listing).

As you see with ESMT + DDR2 bottlenecks, the operating income they get from just securing wafers during shortages and doing fabless models is incredible. 

And it would make more sense to fund this with cashflow down the road.

- NASDAQ listing ongoing. CFO gave a very lawyer like answer, but on track as usual.

- "We do not see production capacity as a bottleneck at this point in time"

This is very meaningful since with their new foundry partners, implies $SIVE is coming online with a very material CW laser supply to a bottlenecked market.

TLDR:
- NEW substantial FOUNDRY ALLOCATION! (very, very material during CW laser shortage)
- 6 new pluggable players outside of $JBL 
- Clear revenue ramp timelines from Jabil

Heavy focus on pluggables -> NPO -> CPO seems like the progression.  Only lukewarm piece was building up internal capacity but it's long term positive.  

Anyway, very happy after reading the transcript aside from potential capex prioritizing laser capacity (which is fine too during an industry shortage) over IP acquisition.

The 6 new pluggable players + substantial wafer allocation "available now" is a pretty insane disclosure.

In seven or eight years there'll be gigantic hedge funds that nobody can see. They wont have an office or a star trader on the front page of the FT... the whole operation will be agents running capital through the liquidity layer.

Think about what a hedge fund is. A group of managers allocating capital to pods of traders. Every one of those pods can be an agent on chain... your relative value bond agent, your equity arb agent, your long short agent. That alone strips out something like 90% of the cost of allocating capital.

Then the mothership. Risk management, compliance, capital raising... AI eats all of that too. You can apply it to every asset management business on earth. 

An invisible economy is coming, and all of it inevitably happens onchain. DeFi is the obvious venue.

Most VCs prefer serial entrepreneurs.

I don't.

I back first-time entrepreneurs more than most.

Yes, it's riskier, but the returns can be much bigger.

Second-time entrepreneurs are usually better operationally. They make sure they raise the RIGHT amount of money. They're ruthless about hiring.

But first-time entrepreneurs? They tend to raise too much money. They feel like they have to hire everybody. Then they hit the wall and wonder why the next round didn't come as easily.

Second-time entrepreneurs who've hit the wall know to keep it thin until product-market fit. Grow organically. Don't rely on the venture capital marketplace because it comes and goes.

I like first-time entrepreneurs making this their career. This might be the one they were meant to be.

I like second-time entrepreneurs going after something entirely different. Not recreating their old business.

Bill Gates, Steve Jobs, Mark Zuckerberg, Larry Ellison… first-time entrepreneurs.

Who do you choose to die?

Reserve Bank of Kansas City (sponsor of Jackson Hole) titled this year's theme as "Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy."

So ignorant media hosts like Dani Burger said it would be sooo disappointing if Warsh talks about Stablecoins?

Wrong!

Here's why...

3 key points that need to be wrapped together to understand the future of the global monetary system:

1) Increased Treasury buybacks are just the beginning of a more activist Bessent. Prior to his appointment as SecTres, he stated prominently that he wanted to be a part of the remaking the global financial order in a way that has not been done since Bretton Woods. He's beginning to act on that desire. 

2) Warsh talked more about reducing the balance sheet prior to his appointment than about hiking rates. At the time, many saw this as negative for the debasement trade: gold, BTC, etc. How wrong those thoughts are.

3) Warsh is expected to spend at least some time tomorrow am on stablecoins. Many think that topic doesn't relate to rising rates and the fiscal situation. Once again, how wrong those thoughts are.

Putting this all together:

The debt and specifically the net interest expense have gotten out of control. US must bring down it's cost of borrowing. As I posted earlier this week, there is a simple way to do this. Buyback higher coupon notes/bonds and reissue bills (short-term debt).

But who will buy all these T-Bills? And how does that relate to the Fed's balance sheet as well as stablecoins?

There is a huge demand for Bills, but if the Treasury really wants to fund itself with Bills going forward, it will need much more demand. Enter the balance sheet and stablecoins.

Stablecoins buy bills: That is an easy one. But seeing the connection to the Fed balance sheet is trickier, but not really.

Very simply, it's called a balance sheet b/c assets (+SH equity) must equal liabilities.

What are the Fed's assets? Mortgages and Treasuries mostly.

What are the Fed's liabilities? Mostly bank reserves and some paper bills.

Thus, if Warsh wants to reduce the Fed balance sheet, he can't simply start selling (or stop rolling) over current assets. Assets must equate to liabilities. This is why Powell restarted QE earlier this year with a Bill buying program. So that banks could keep more reserves with the Fed. 

Thus, Warsh must also significantly reduce liabilities should he wish to reduce assets. In other words, he must force banks to lower reserves.

So, and this is a bit complicated, but I will boil it down here. Warsh will need to force banks out of reserves. The closest monetary cousin to reserves, is, you guessed it, T-Bills.

Thus, a massive shortening of Treasury duration is underway, shifting even more the $40T in debt to the short end. But there must be buyers: The banks and stablecoins.

Warsh speaking on stablecoins tomorrow is not some unrelated topic to the major issues of today. It is the topic.
